scope: Forefoot additions and site instantiation for existing diabetic-foot infection/report fields; no blanket plantar-plate tear or instability examination.

RA.supports: Ulcer-to-bone/joint routes and site-directed foot MRI coverage; examination planes and contrast limitations.

IWGDF.supports: Recommendation 8 and rationale: MRI for unresolved suspected osteomyelitis, with soft-tissue/bone/joint extent and specificity limitations.

EANM.supports: Soft-tissue infection extent, abscesses and tenosynovitis; forefoot spread can cross compartments.

LESSER_MTP_2003.supports: 48 lesser MTP joints: plate, capsule, collateral complexes and attachments; figures2–3 relate flexor/extensor tendons and intermetatarsal bursa. MR arthrography improved some details; do not import that visibility into routine MRI.

HALLUX_2020.supports: Hallux capsulosesamoid complex and metatarsosesamoid articulations; supporting tendons and separate collateral structures. Not interchangeable with lesser plates.

HALLUX_2021.supports: Nine cadaveric feet; figures2/3/5/7 identify the central portion, intersesamoid and paired sesamoid ligaments and supporting tendons. Authors explicitly differ from older descriptions of the central portion.

HALLUX_2002.supports: Hallux articular/periarticular anatomy, cartilage, sesamoid ligaments and named tendon attachments.

TENOSYNOVITIS_2017.supports: Evaluated named bone and tendon disease against surgery/histopathology; supports explicit tendon/sheath infection mapping, not universal clinical accuracy.

FDB_VARIATION_2005.supports: FDB fifth-toe anatomy varies; missing or small components must not be fabricated from a standard atlas.

FDB_ANATOMY_2017.supports: FDB digit-specific slips and middle-phalangeal attachments, with observed fifth-slip absence.

proposed_expansion_rules.rule: Map each actual ulcer/tract separately through named tissues to specific bone, joint, sheath or collection; incomplete coverage remains explicit and unverified.

Use explicit14 MTP/IP site pairs. A named joint leaf does not itself instantiate opposing cartilage, synovium or bone-surface requirements. Distal hallux has one IP joint; do not create hallux middle phalanx/PIP/DIP.
Preserve hallux-versus-lesser anatomy and label normal reference material as a reference. A source slice showing one component cannot cover a whole plate, all attachments or a contralateral digit.

Separate tendon substance from its actual synovial sheath or other investing tissue. Do not propagate ankle synovial-sheath coverage to the entire distal extensor course; Achilles paratenon is not a universal tendon sheath. A generic tendon-group image does not instantiate every digit.

A compartment label cannot substitute for named contents; forefoot spread may cross compartments. Preserve imaged stump, resection margins, residual tendons and altered routes. Not every source model has every compartment or postoperative variant.

non_destructive_refinement_requests.issue: Eight different tendon records share a generic sheath-or-Achilles label.
non_destructive_refinement_requests.proposal: Retain IDs for traceability while distinguishing synovial sheath at the demonstrated segment from paratenon/peritendinous tissues; create explicit digit instances for FDL/EDL. Only Achilles may use an Achilles-paratenon label. Do not invent a continuous distal extensor synovial sheath.

non_destructive_refinement_requests.issue: Generic named-muscle placeholder is not completed by these tendon additions.
non_destructive_refinement_requests.proposal: Keep blocked until actual named muscle/site inventory and source acquisition are supplied.
Identify actual members for the involved route; no normal bundle or vascular viability coverage is granted by forefoot pictures.

unresolved_review_questions: MSK specialist reconciliation of source-dependent central hallux plantar portion terminology and attachment boundaries.
Exact synovial-sheath segment mapping for every named tendon remains separate from the additive digit-flexor proposal.

IP plantar/collateral stabilizers, digital pulley detail, deep transverse ligament subdivision and every intrinsic muscle/neurovascular branch are not exhaustively specified by this bounded proposal; existing broad scope remains unresolved.
No acquisition-specific MRI proof or commercial asset approval exists merely because these requirement IDs or anatomical names are present.
Cadaveric MRI, in-vivo MRI, ultrasound, histology and schematics must remain individually typed; ultrasound or histology cannot satisfy an MRI-specific image leaf.
